new.title: Target OS version for Automated Device Enrollment
new.text: Automated Device Enrollment now has an update to setting in addition to the minimum required OS version, so you can set a floor for enrollment and a separate version that devices update to. Devices below the minimum update to that version before they enroll, and devices already at or above the minimum enroll without updating. This works for macOS, iOS, and iPadOS, and existing configurations keep their current behavior.

new.text: The Single Sign-On Library Item now supports OpenID sign-in on macOS 27 and later, so users can sign in through identity provider web sign-in pages, including multi-factor authentication, at the login window, Lock Screen, and FileVault unlock. New settings let you sync the web login password to the local account and set a web login URL allow list. These settings apply only to Macs running macOS 27 or later, and OpenID depends on the identity provider supporting it.

new.title: Recommended privacy permissions for Mac
new.text:
The Privacy Library Item's Recommended privacy permissions area now supports Mac, in addition to iPhone and iPad. Admins can recommend app permissions for macOS apps and website permissions for Safari, so end users see a single consent prompt listing everything an app or site needs instead of being prompted one permission at a time. The user can select Allow to grant every recommended permission at once, or Not Now, in which case the app continues to prompt for individual permissions as it normally would.
Supported Mac app permissions include Bluetooth, Camera, Dictation, Local Network, Location, and Microphone. Mac apps are identified by bundle ID and code requirement, and a recommendation applies only when the installed app's code signature matches. Website rules use the same specific and wildcard domains as iPhone and iPad. This requires Macs on macOS 27 or later.
For more details, see Configure the Privacy Library Item.

Why is managing work email, calendars, and contacts difficult across devices?
Manual account setup and inconsistent device configurations create recurring work for IT administrators. Each operating system, application, and service provider introduces requirements that administrators must address before employees can use their work accounts.
Consider a new employee who can receive email but cannot access team calendars or essential contacts. The mailbox works, yet the employee still needs separate support requests to complete their setup. Repeating this process across departments makes onboarding harder to standardize.
Effective email, calendar, and contact management requires a defined configuration for each device environment. IT teams need to distribute the appropriate settings centrally while accounting for corporate and personal ownership, enrollment methods, and the services employees already use.

Why does app distribution become difficult as device fleets grow?
The app catalog vs app group distinction helps IT teams separate application discovery from application organization. As device fleets grow, overlapping requirements make it harder to decide which apps belong together, how employees receive them, and who needs them. A clear distribution structure lets administrators reuse application sets while distinguishing mandatory installations from optional tools.
App distribution becomes difficult when IT teams manage overlapping application requirements without separating app organization, deployment behavior, and target audiences. Administrators must determine which apps belong together, how installation should happen, and who needs them.
Consider an administrator selecting applications for new hires, adjusting software after department transfers, and handling optional installation requests. Across Windows, macOS, Android, and iOS, these tasks involve different application packages and installation requirements. new.title: How to introduce AI agents into IT operations with human oversight?
new.text:
AI agents in IT operations can interpret requests, determine next steps, and execute authorized actions across endpoint, identity, and ticketing systems. However, a single incorrect action can affect multiple systems before an administrator intervenes.
Human-in-the-loop oversight involves human participation in an AI-driven workflow through activities such as supervision, feedback, intervention, or approval at appropriate decision points. To introduce AI agents safely, IT teams must define permissions, establish approval checkpoints, monitor execution, handle failures, and expand autonomy gradually.
What Are the Risks of AI Agents in IT Operations?
AI agents in IT operations introduce four key risks: excessive permissions, unapproved actions, incomplete audit trails, and unclear failure ownership. These gaps can leave administrators unable to contain changes, reconstruct events, or determine who must resolve a failed workflow.
Excessive permissions: An LLM-based agent receives administrator-level access when its task only requires reading device inventory. OWASP classifies excessive permissions, functionality, and autonomy as contributing causes of the Excessive Agency vulnerability.
Unapproved high-impact actions: An agent isolates a production endpoint without human approval, disrupting critical business operations.
Incomplete audit trails: An agent modifies security policies without recording the initiating request, approval decision, or execution outcome.

new.title: Known issue: OS update information and OS update installation on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS 27
new.text:
Apple removed the commands that Miradore used to find and install OS updates. Learn how this affects your Apple devices and what to do now.
In this article
Toggle
Description
Apple removed the older MDM commands that Miradore used to find and install OS updates. This change affects iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27. Apple now manages OS updates with Declarative Device Management (DDM).
Because of this, you might see the following issues:
The list of available OS updates on the Device page is wrong or incomplete
Devices on version 27: A device upgraded from version 26 can still show updates from before the upgrade. For example, a Mac on macOS 27.0 can list macOS 26.7 and 27.0 as available. A device enrolled directly on version 27 lists no updates.
Devices on version 26 or earlier: Version 27 does not appear as an available update. The device can look up to date when a newer version exists.
Dashboards and reports show the same wrong data
The iOS and macOS System update status widgets, the OS update reports, and custom reports that use Apple OS update fields show incorrect data.
The Software update action does not work on iPhone and iPad devices that run iOS 27 or iPadOS 27
The Software update action has no effect and you also cannot use it to upgrade devices from version 26 to version 27. These devices now need a declaration to install OS updates. The upcoming Software update settings configuration profile includes that declaration. For more information on the configuration profile, see the Status section.
Patch management cannot be used to install macOS updates on devices running macOS 27
When trying to install OS updates via patch management, the action has no effect on the devices.
The device inventory still shows the correct OS version. Only the list of updates and their installation are affected.
Affected services
OS update information
Available OS update information is affected on all iPhone, iPad, and Mac devices as follows:
Devices running iOS 27, iPadOS 27, or macOS 27: The available OS updates list is out of date or empty.
Devices running version 26 or earlier: Version 27 is not shown as an available update.
The following areas show incorrect data:
Available OS updates on the Device page
System update status widgets for iOS and macOS
OS update reports and custom reports that use Apple OS update fields
Software update action
The Software update action (available in the Premium and Premium+ plans) is affected on iPhone and iPad devices that meet the following conditions:
The device is supervised.
The device is running iOS 27 or iPadOS 27, or you want to upgrade it from version 26 to version 27.
OS update installation via patch management
OS update installation with Mac patch management (available in the Premium and Premium+ plans) is affected on devices that run macOS 27.
Application patches for Mac devices, for example for Adobe, Zoom, or Dropbox, are not affected.
Status
We are moving OS update management for Apple devices to DDM, which is how Apple supports OS update management from version 27 onward. Miradore turns DDM on automatically, so you do not need to do anything.
Fixes and new functionality are planned to be delivered as follows:
iOS and iPadOS
DDM support and a new Software update settings configuration profile reach production in the next couple of weeks. These functionalities require iOS 18 or iPadOS 18 or later installed on the devices. The configuration profile also brings new capabilities for iPhone and iPad devices that were not possible before:
Enforce OS updates: You can make devices download and install OS updates and security updates automatically, without asking the device user.
Block or allow automatic updates: For each setting, you can turn it always on, always off, or leave the choice to the device user.
Delay OS updates: You can hide new OS updates from device users for 1 to 90 days after Apple releases them.
Choose which updates users see: When several updates are available, you can show all of them, only the oldest, or only the newest.
Available OS updates on the Device page
In the coming weeks, Miradore will get update data directly from Apple instead of the device. The Device page, the System update status widgets, and the reports will then show correct data for iOS, iPadOS, and macOS devices.
macOS
This fix takes some more weeks. It restores OS update installation from Mac patch management on macOS 27.
New: major macOS upgrades
We are adding a way to upgrade Mac devices to a new major macOS version from Miradore. For example, you can upgrade from macOS 26 to macOS 27. This is currently not possible in Miradore.
We will update this article as each fix is released.
What you can do in the meantime
As a workaround until we release the fixes and new functionalities, you can do the following to ensure your devices remain up to date:
Check the OS version in the device inventory to see which version a device runs. Do not use the list of available OS updates for any Apple device until the fix is released.
Ask device users to install updates on their own devices by navigating to the following menus:
iPhone and iPad: Settings > General > Software Update
Mac: System Settings > General > Software Update
We apologize for the trouble this may have caused you.

new.title: End of support for devices running macOS versions below macOS 12 (Monterey)
new.text:
As of 14 October, 2026, we no longer provide support for devices running OS versions below macOS 12.
The change does not affect currently enrolled devices and some functionalities remain operational on lower macOS versions. However, only devices running macOS 12 or later can be enrolled in Miradore.
In this article
Toggle
Why are we raising the official minimum supported macOS version?
To keep Miradore up to date with the latest platform requirements and security standards, we are raising our official support for macOS devices from version 10.7 (OS X Lion) to 12 (Monterey).
This change is the result of our updating the .NET framework, which affects the Miradore client and is needed to keep it secure. With the new .NET version, we can no longer support devices running OS versions below macOS 12.
For increased security and the best user experience, we always recommend using the latest operating system available.
Miradore client update (version 1.6.8)
As part of this change, we are releasing Miradore client version 1.6.8 (Build 147) for macOS devices. This is a maintenance release required for future platform compatibility — it does not introduce new features.
The update is delivered through the App Store and does not require any admin action. The timing depends on each device's settings:
If automatic app updates are enabled and the device is connected to a Wi-Fi network, the update typically installs within a few hours or overnight.
If automatic app updates are enabled and the device uses cellular data, it might wait to connect to a Wi-Fi network before installing the update within a few hours or overnight.
If automatic app updates are disabled, device users must update the Miradore client from the App Store manually.
Devices running macOS versions older than macOS 12 that already have the client installed will continue to work, but they will not receive this or future client updates.
What does this mean for devices running older macOS versions?
Nothing is being actively blocked at this time, and existing device management functionality may continue to work on older versions.
Devices running versions older than macOS 12 are no longer officially supported by Miradore, which means we cannot guarantee that all features will work as expected on those devices.
Miradore client version 1.6.8 (Build 147) cannot be installed on devices running versions older than macOS 12. Devices that already have an older version of the client installed will continue to work but will not receive future updates. This may impact features that depend on the macOS client, such as app and patch management.
We strongly recommend upgrading older devices to macOS 12 or newer whenever possible.
Which platforms are supported?
Miradore continues to support the following operating system platforms:
Android 7 and later
iOS 13 and later
iPadOS 13 and later
macOS 12 and later
Windows 7, 8, 10, and 11
If you have any questions or concerns, don't hesitate to reach out to your Account Manager or our Support team.

new.title: overview
new.text:
Overview
The Overview section provides a snapshot of critical metrics for effective update management. It consists of three main components:
Dashboard
A centralized display presenting key update management data and insights:
Updates Status:
This bar chart provides a comprehensive view of the overall update status across all devices, helping to quickly identify the gap between Eligible, Installed, Pending, and Failed updates. The chart uses different colors for each bar: Green for Eligible Updates, Dark Green for Installed Updates, Yellow for Pending Updates, and Dark Red for Failed Updates. It visually represents the following:
Eligible Updates: This represents the overall eligible update count. Hovering over this bar displays the count of eligible updates.
Installed Updates: Represents the overall installed update count. Hovering over this bar displays the count of installed updates.
Pending Updates: Represents the count of (Deployed + Pending Updates) that are not installed. Hovering over this bar displays the count of pending updates.
Failed Updates: Represents the count of updates which did not succeed on devices. Hovering over this bar displays the count of failed updates.
Updates Distribution: This nested donut chart displays the distribution of OS updates.
Updates Pending: This line chart illustrates the trend of updates pending installation on devices over the past 30 days, highlighting patterns and daily milestones. The X-axis represents the time split over the last 7 days, while the Y-axis shows the cumulative count of updates deployed during this period. The chart includes three lines for Installed Updates, Pending Updates, and Failed Updates, with daily milestones indicated. Hovering over these milestones displays the update count with pending updates. Chart controls allow for maximizing the view and refreshing the data to show only the most recent 30 days.
Overview Tiles
Visual elements summarizing essential metrics and statuses:
Eligible Updates: The total count of eligible updates for installation
Installed Updates: The total count of successfully installed updates.
Pending Updates: The count of updates that are pending for installation.
Failed Updates: The count of updates that have failed installation.
Table List Details
Following are the updates identified by the device as available but have not yet been installed:
Published Date: Represents the date when the update was published.
Details: Provides additional details about the update.
Classification: Provides information about the OS Updates.
Installed Devices: Displays the count of devices where the update is installed.
Eligible Devices: Displays the count of devices that are eligible for the update.
Pending Devices: Displays the count of devices where the update has been applied but is still awaiting installation.
Failed Devices: Shows the count of devices where the update failed to install after retries.
note
Users can click on the Eligible Devices Count, Installed Devices, Pending Devices, and Failed Devices hyperlinks to view detailed information.
The following are the other options available on the overview page:
Set as default: Users can select a default platform (iOS, Windows, Linux, or macOS) by checking the 'Set as default' option. Once a platform is set as the default, the checkbox will be selected and disabled. To change the default, users can navigate to another platform from the dropdown menu, where the 'Set Default Platform' checkbox can be enabled.
Export: Exports the table data to be saved locally in CSV format.
Search Box: Allows users to search for specific information.
Refresh Icon: Updates the table with real-time data.

new.title: automated software updates
new.text:
Automated Software Updates is an advanced software update management capability in SureMDM for iOS/iPadOS that enables organizations to manage and deploy iOS/iPadOS updates across devices in a controlled and automated manner. This feature helps IT administrators streamline update management, maintain device security, minimize disruptions, and ensure iOS/iPadOS devices remain up to date with the latest supported software versions.
note
This feature is applicable to iOS 18.0 and later and is available to Premium-tier customers and above.
Enabling Automated Software Updates
When accessing the Automated Software Updates section for the first time, the feature is disabled by default.
Navigate to SureMDM Console > OS Updates > iOS/iPadOS > Automated Software Updates.
Click Enable Automated Software Updates.
Once enabled:
Automated Software Updates becomes active which has the following two sections:
Overview
Configuration
The system automatically creates the following four default deployment rings and five charts:
Canary Ring
Early Adopters Ring
Broad Rollout Ring
General Availability Ring
Device with No Ring Assigned - (Available only as chart)
These default rings can be reviewed and configured from the Configuration tab.

new.title: add new ring
new.text:
Administrators can create custom deployment rings to control how and when iOS updates are rolled out across devices. In addition to the four system-defined default rings, administrators can create up to 15 custom rings, resulting in a maximum of 19 rings (default + custom).

Navigate to SureMDM Console > OS Updates > iOS/iPadOS > Automated Software Updates > Configuration.
Click Add New Ring.
The Add New Ring configuration screen opens.
Add New Ring – Configuration Sections
The Add New Ring screen is organized into multiple sections. Each section must be reviewed and configured before saving the ring.
1. Ring Details
This section defines the identity and purpose of the ring.
FieldDescription
Ring Name
Enter a unique name for the ring. This name is used across the Configuration table, Overview charts, and reports.
Description
Optional. Provide a brief description explaining the intent or target audience of the ring (for example, pilot users or specific departments).
2. Configuration Details
Update Settings
This section determines which iOS updates are eligible for deployment through the ring.
OptionDescription
Automatic Software Update Action Management
Automatic Download of Available Updates
Allows administrators to enable or disable automatic downloading of available updates on the device. Select from the following options:
Allowed (Default)
Always On
Always Off
Automatic Installation of OS Updates

Allowed
Always On
Always Off

Scheduled – Devices that are assigned the update but for which the update process has not yet started.
Download In-Progress – Devices that are currently downloading the update package.
Prepared for Installation – Devices where the update has been downloaded and prepared and is ready for installation.

Platform SSO is a macOS capability that integrates local Mac sign-in with Microsoft Entra ID and enables single sign-on to supported organizational applications and websites. Depending on the selected authentication method, it can use a Secure Enclave-backed key, a smart card, or the user's Microsoft Entra password.
SureMDM provides two configuration areas for setting up this integration:
Extensible SSO Configuration: Configures the Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in, including its extension identifier, Team Identifier, authentication type, and associated URLs.
Platform SSO Configuration: Enables Platform SSO and defines the authentication method and user registration behavior.

new.title: post enrollment
new.text:
Post-enrollment registration allows administrators to configure Microsoft Entra Platform Single Sign-On (Platform SSO) on macOS devices that are already enrolled and managed through SureMDM. This approach enables organizations to extend Platform SSO capabilities to existing devices without requiring them to be re-enrolled.
Administrators can configure the required Extensible SSO and Platform SSO settings in a macOS profile and deploy it to the enrolled devices through the SureMDM console. Once the profile is installed, users can complete the Microsoft Entra registration process directly on their Macs.
Prerequisites
Before configuring Platform SSO in SureMDM, ensure that the following requirements are met.
Supported macOS version: macOS 14 Sonoma or later is recommended for Platform SSO.
Microsoft Company Portal: Install a compatible version of the Microsoft Company Portal app. Microsoft specifies version 5.2404.0 or later for Platform SSO.
Microsoft Entra ID permissions: Users must have the necessary permissions to register or join devices to Microsoft Entra ID.
Microsoft Authenticator: Ensure it is available and configured as required by your organization's authentication and multifactor authentication policies.
Network access: Ensure that the device can reach the required Microsoft Entra authentication endpoints.
Refer to the Microsoft Platform SSO prerequisites for the latest requirements.
Steps to Configure Extensible SSO in SureMDM
Navigate to Profiles → macOS → Select Enrollment Type → Access Identity & Access Management → Extensible SSO → Configure.
Step 1: SSO Configuration tab
In this section, configure the options as mentioned below:
SettingsDescription
SSO Provider

OS Update
The OS Update Job helps the admin remotely initiate and manage OS version upgrades on enrolled Android device(s), ensuring seamless and consistent updates across the fleet.

A Uri of the file that contains the update. Before uploading the ‘Update file URL’, ensure that the firmware package is bootable via Android Debug Bridge (ADB) sideload to avoid bricking the device.

new.title: New Features and Enhancements > Per-Device Declaration Status — Jamf Pro 11.33.0
new.text:
For compatible Jamf Cloud environments, you can now view the status of every declaration deployed to a device from the Declarations pane in a device's Inventory tab. Use the status to verify and troubleshoot blueprint deployments from a single device record.
For each declaration, you can view the component it maps to, the declaration type, the delivery channel, the source, and the status. When a status displays a View link, select it to open the Reason details window and view the reason for the unsuccessful status.
The Declarations pane displays status only. You cannot deploy or edit blueprints from this view. To create or edit a blueprint, click Blueprints in the sidebar.
Note:
This feature is also available in Jamf Pro 11.32.0.

new.text:
To prepare for Jamf App Catalog app deployments in blueprints, Jamf Pro now automatically delivers a Privacy Preferences Policy Control configuration profile granting Full Disk Access to Self Service+ and its bundled binaries during enrollment. The profile is scoped to the Self Service+ bundle ID (com.jamf.selfserviceplus), consistent with the existing App Installers Privacy Preferences Policy Control profile.
A new Declarative Device Management Migration Guide is available to help administrators determine when and how to migrate certain workflows to blueprints.

new.title: Important Notices > Notice History by Release — Jamf Pro 11.33.0
new.text:
Starting with version...Change or ConsiderationDescription
11.31.0
Upcoming New Privileges for Mass Actions
In an upcoming release, new privileges for mass actions will be added to Jamf Pro. Previously, performing a mass action only required the corresponding privilege for a single device. This change will limit high-impact actions to the administrators and API clients that require them. These privileges will not be added to any existing account automatically, and they will not be included in the "Administrator" privilege set. If your organization needs an account or API client to perform these actions, you will need to create or update a custom privilege set and explicitly grant the privileges.
To prepare for this change, Jamf recommends you review any accounts and API clients that currently perform mass lock, wipe, unmanage, or delete actions on computers or mobile devices, and plan to grant the new privileges through a custom privilege set once the release is available.
11.31.0
Self Service+ for Mobile Release
Self Service+ for mobile was released 20 July 2026 on the App Store for Apple devices. Devices with iOS or iPadOS 16.x or earlier will remain on Self Service 11.4.2.
Self Service+ for mobile expands on the Self Service experience when you create and deploy an activation profile using Jamf Security Cloud, enabling network security monitoring, threat alerts, and centralized notifications in addition to the Self Service capabilities that Jamf Pro enables.
For more information, including deployment instructions and requirements, see the Self Service+ for Mobile Deployment Guide.
11.29.0
macOS Version Reporting Inconsistency
A known issue in Jamf Pro causes a computer's macOS version to be reported inconsistently, affecting smart group and advanced search membership. The macOS version could be reported as a two-part version (e.g., 13.3) or a three-part version (e.g., 13.3.0), depending on the source of the inventory data. This inconsistency can cause computers to be temporarily added or removed from smart groups and advanced searches unexpectedly.
Jamf Pro 11.31.0 now reports the macOS version consistently as a two-part version when patch versions are not expressed in the version reported from macOS (e.g., 13.3). Jamf Pro will continue to correctly report three-part patch versions as expected.

new.title: Deprecations and Removals — Jamf Pro 11.33.0
new.text:
Deprecations Added in This Release
DeprecationNotes
AFP for File Share Distribution Points
Apple has removed support for the Apple Filing Protocol (AFP) starting in macOS 27. Computers with macOS 27 or later will fail to mount file share distribution points using AFP. Jamf recommends that you transition existing distribution points to use SMB or enable HTTPS.
Deprecations Added in a Previous Release
DeprecationNotes
Non-OIDC-based administrator authentication methods for cloud-hosted Jamf Pro instances
In a future release of Jamf Pro (estimated target: the second half of 2027), support for the following legacy administrator authentication methods will be removed:
Local Jamf Pro accounts
SAML-based authentication (including failover login URLs)
LDAP and directory service-based authentication
After the removal, Jamf Pro will require an OIDC-based authentication method to log in, such as Jamf ID or federation through an OIDC-compliant identity provider.
Migrating to platform authentication improves the security of your Jamf Pro environment while enabling additional platform functionality. It also ensures readiness for Apple's upcoming removal of legacy MDM software update commands by enabling the declarative device management capabilities in blueprints.
Jamf recommends migrating to a supported authentication method as soon as possible. For more information or assistance with migrating, contact your Account team.
Note:
This deprecation specifically applies to administrator login for cloud-hosted Jamf Pro instances. Self-hosted instances will not be affected.
Jamf plans to introduce replacement options for fallback access functionality in Jamf Pro before failover URLs are removed.
DigiCert PKI Platform 8 support
DigiCert PKI Platform 8 (mPKI8) end of issuance was 01 October 2025. Jamf Pro is undergoing a phased approach to this deprecation. The ability to create new mPKI8 integrations is removed. In a future release of Jamf Pro, all mPKI8 integrations and associated information (e.g., certificate deployment records) will be removed from the Jamf Pro database.
For more information on the end of issuance, see the following documentation from DigiCert:
Transitioning certificate issuance from PKI Platform 8 to DigiCert® ONE
Rackspace and Akamai cloud distribution point support
Support for distribution points hosted in Rackspace or Akamai Cloud will be removed in a future release of Jamf Pro. If your environment uses a distribution point hosted by either of these providers, Jamf recommends migrating your content to a different hosting solution, such as the Jamf Cloud Distribution Service (JCDS). Contact Jamf Support for additional information.
Self Service classic for macOS support
Self Service classic for macOS is deprecated as of 31 March 2026, meaning it will no longer receive new features or bug fixes but remains available for use. Administrators are advised to migrate to Self Service+, the new end user application, which provides the same core functionality as Self Service classic while enabling new integrations with other Jamf applications such as Jamf Connect.
Note:
While Self Service classic will no longer receive updates or bug fixes, it will continue to be deployed to computers that are unable to run Self Service+, such as those running versions earlier than macOS 13. Self Service classic continues to be available via automatic deployment if Use Self Service+ as the default end user application is not enabled. All options related to Self Service classic will continue to be available in Jamf Pro, but they will no longer be maintained.
Software identification (SWID) tags
The functionality to use software identification (SWID) tags for licensed software records will be removed.
Maintenance pages
Functionality to make policies available offline
This option, currently available only for policies set to the "Ongoing" frequency, will be removed from the Jamf Pro interface, and all policies will require a connection to the Jamf Pro server to check for triggers before running.
Sign QuickAdd Package functionality for user-initiated enrollment settings
This functionality is only used in legacy enrollment workflows involving QuickAdd packages and does not affect the user-initiated enrollment workflow. Estimated removal date: November 2026.
Azure AD Graph for Conditional Access
Azure AD Graph is deprecated. If you previously modified the conditionalAccessDomains.json file, Jamf recommends editing the file to add the "msGraphResourceUrl": "https://graph.microsoft.com/" property into GLOBAL settings and "msGraphResourceUrl": "https://graph.microsoft.us/" into US_GOVERNMENT settings. For more information on this deprecation, see the following documentation from Microsoft:
Migrate your apps from Azure AD Graph to Microsoft Graph
Cache name setting
This setting will be removed from the Single Sign-On Extensions payload in computer and mobile device configuration profiles because Apple deprecated them.
Password expiration and Replication time settings
These settings will be removed from the Single Sign-On Extensions payload in computer configuration profiles because Apple deprecated them.
Skip Display Tone and Skip Home button sensitivity settings
These settings will be removed from the Skip Setup Items payload for mobile device configuration profiles.
Home Button Sensitivity and True Tone Display settings
These settings will be removed from the General payload for computer and mobile device PreStage enrollments.
Functionality to issue the Tomcat SSL/TLS certificate from Jamf Pro's built-in certificate authority
Jamf Pro's functionality to issue the Tomcat SSL/TLS certificate from the JSS built-in certificate authority (CA) will be discontinued. The release version for this change has not been determined. Before this change occurs, it is recommended that all on-premise Jamf Pro instances leveraging this functionality switch to a publicly trusted third-party CA to issue the Tomcat SSL/TLS certificate. This will prevent the potential loss of MDM communication from Jamf Pro to enrolled devices. If needed, a Tomcat SSL/TLS server certificate for Jamf Pro may be issued from an internal certificate authority. The JSS built-in CA will maintain its current ability to manually issue server certificates to other servers.
The "DIGEST-MD5" authentication type option
"DIGEST-MD5" will be removed from the authentication type options. This authentication type option displays when configuring an LDAP server to use Jamf Infrastructure Manager as a proxy server.
Computer Access Only and Mobile Device Access Only Limited Access settings
Jamf Pro web app instances with one of these settings configured will automatically be updated to the Computer and Mobile Device Access setting. Administrators will only be able to assign Full Access or Computer and Mobile Device Access privileges after the deprecation.
Webhook responses for ComputerPolicyFinished and ComputerCheckIn
These webhook responses will be modified to include additional information. These changes may break integrations that currently utilize these event types.
Supervise Devices and Make MDM Profile Mandatory settings in a mobile device PreStage enrollment
The ability to supervise devices and require the user to install the MDM Profile during enrollment with a PreStage enrollment will be required and will be built-in functionality. These settings will be removed from the Jamf Pro user interface.

Support for non-certificate based client communication with the Jamf Pro server

new.title: Scalefusion October 9th, 2026 Release Notes
new.text:
Version Information
Scalefusion Dashboard: v68.3.0
Release Notes
1. Remote Cast and Control for Linux Devices
Scalefusion now supports remote viewing and control for Linux devices through the RCV2 platform. This release includes the following capabilities:
a. Multi-admin support: Allows multiple administrators to participate in remote sessions.
b. Unmute to call: Supports unmuting audio during a remote session.
c. Annotations: Enables administrators to use annotation tools during remote sessions.
Note: Remote access requires end-user participation. The end user must grant permission to inject key events and select the screen to share. File transfer is not supported.
2. Webhooks Support for SIEM Events
Webhooks have been extended to support SIEM-related events, including the events available through Splunk and QRadar integrations. Organizations can configure Webhooks to send these events to their SIEM tools, provided the tools support Webhook consumption. The enhancement includes the following:
a. Header-based authentication: Configure Webhooks with a Bearer token, an Authorization header, or other custom key-value headers to authenticate requests received by the SIEM tool.
b. Firewall configuration: If the SIEM tool is behind a firewall, the applicable Scalefusion Smokescreen IP address for the organization's instance must be allowlisted.
3. Private Splunk Integration
Scalefusion now supports integration with private Splunk instances hosted behind a firewall that cannot be exposed to the internet.
a. Splunk extension: Install the Scalefusion-provided extension in Splunk to establish communication with the Scalefusion cloud instance. The extension initiates outbound calls from Splunk, eliminating the need to allowlist incoming connections from Scalefusion.
b. Developer API: Organizations can also configure private Splunk using the Developer API and a Developer API key, without using the extension.
Note: Support for Splunk integration through the Developer API is not provided. Support is available only for integrations using the Scalefusion-provided Splunk extension.
4.Windows OS Upgrade Support for Windows 11, Version 26H2
Windows OS Upgrade now supports upgrading eligible devices to Windows 11, version 26H2.
5. iOS App Configuration APIs
Scalefusion Developer APIs for creating, editing, deleting, and querying app configurations have been extended to iOS. These APIs enable IT administrators to manage iOS app configurations dynamically through their developer tools and systems.

new.title: October 14th, 2026
new.text:
New: Agent Uninstall Protection
Feature: Device Management
Prevent unauthorized removal of the JumpCloud agent so your devices stay managed. Agent Uninstall Protection is on by default for all devices running JumpCloud agent v2.179.2 or later. Uninstalling the agent with standard methods on macOS, Windows, and Linux now requires a per-device maintenance token.
Directory Insights Events: Directory Insights logs failed uninstall attempts, successful uninstalls, and exemption policy changes, identifying the device and the user.
Maintenance Tokens: Admins with Manager role permissions or higher can view a device's maintenance token from the device details. Tokens work without network connectivity and automatically rotate 60 minutes after they're viewed if the agent remains installed.
Exemption Policies: Use the Disable Agent Uninstall Protection policy for macOS, Windows, or Linux to remove the token requirement from specific devices during agent maintenance, troubleshooting, or imaging.
Protection Status: View each device's protection status (On, Off, or Failed) from the device details or the Devices list.
Deleting an active device from the Admin Portal or the JumpCloud API still removes the agent without a maintenance token.
Available in the Admin Portal: Go to Device Management > Devices > Settings > Agent Uninstall Protection.

New: Block macOS Golden Gate Installer Policy
Feature: Policy Management
Use the Block macOS Golden Gate Installer policy to prevent the macOS 27 Golden Gate installer from launching on MDM-enrolled Mac computers. If users download the installer from the App Store or another source, the installer is automatically terminated when they try to launch it. To also keep macOS 27 Golden Gate from appearing in Software Update, defer major OS upgrades in your Patch Management policies for up to 90 days.
